```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 100)
```

This guide runs the experimental allocation workflow from start to finish on
the open Cornwall GP data that ship with spax: prepare inputs, declare a model,
fit it to observed registrations, inspect the saved fit, predict at new
locations and compare a change in one practice's supply. A bootstrap section
then uses generated data, where the true parameters are known, before the
results are exported and read back in a fresh R session.

The model is a corrected static conditional logit (CLM) with an explicit
outside option. Each practice attracts residents in proportion to its supply,
discounted by travel time; the outside option competes with all practices. For
choosing between this model and an FCA index, see [Choosing an FCA index or an
allocation model](model-choice.html). The [preparation
guide](spax-102-data-prep.html) explains counts, units, IDs and missing
travel, and [saved-result inspection](function-naming.html) describes the
standard R methods used below. The interface is experimental.

```{r packages}
library(spax)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The data

`cornwall_lsoa` holds 337 small areas (LSOAs) and the number of their
residents registered with a GP practice anywhere in England. `cornwall_gp`
holds 55 practices with their GP full-time equivalents (FTE).
`cornwall_flows` counts registered residents by small area and practice, and
`cornwall_travel` gives motorised travel minutes between them. Sources and
licences are listed in `system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax")`.

The Isles of Scilly have no road link to the mainland, so their travel times to
mainland practices are `NA`. This guide models mainland Cornwall only and drops
the Scilly small area and practice throughout.

```{r inputs}
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
mainland_area <- !areas$scilly
mainland_gp <- !gp$scilly
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa[mainland_area], gp$practice[mainland_gp]]

# Demand: residents registered with any practice in England.
demand <- setNames(areas$registered[mainland_area], areas$lsoa[mainland_area])
# Supply: GP FTE excluding GPs in training.
supply <- setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg[mainland_gp], gp$practice[mainland_gp])

# Observed flows: registered residents by small area (rows) and practice.
observed <- matrix(0, nrow(travel), ncol(travel), dimnames = dimnames(travel))
keep <- cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% rownames(travel) &
  cornwall_flows$practice %in% colnames(travel)
observed[cbind(cornwall_flows$lsoa[keep], cornwall_flows$practice[keep])] <-
  cornwall_flows$patients[keep]
dim(travel)
c(registered = sum(demand), at_mainland_practices = sum(observed))
```

Registrations are a stock: who is registered where in July 2026, not a count of
visits. Because demand counts every registered resident, the outside option
stands for registration with a practice outside mainland Cornwall (in Devon,
for example, or on the Isles of Scilly). It is not unmet need: almost everyone
is registered with some practice.

## Prepare, declare and fit

`prepare_allocation()` aligns demand, supply and travel by their names and
checks them once. Unit and period labels are declarations attached to the
results; spax does not convert units. `clm_allocation()` then declares the
model: a Gaussian travel kernel with scale σ (minutes) and a fitted outside
weight v0.

```{r prepare}
cornwall_units <- list(
  demand_units = "registered residents", demand_period = "July 2026",
  supply_units = "GP FTE excluding GPs in training", supply_period = "June 2026",
  travel_units = "minutes")
inputs <- prepare_allocation(demand, supply, travel, metadata = cornwall_units)
model <- clm_allocation(inputs, family = "gaussian", fit_v0 = TRUE)
```

`fit_allocation()` runs one fit from each supplied start and keeps the best
converged one. Here the target is the small area × practice flow matrix and
the loss is Poisson, chosen explicitly: asking for counts does not choose a
likelihood. Registrations are not independent event counts, so treat the
Poisson loss as a fitting criterion rather than a full observation model.
Joint Poisson fitting does not force the modelled total to match the observed
total.

```{r fit}
starts <- rbind(near = c(sigma = 3, v0 = 0.05), middle = c(sigma = 6, v0 = 0.01),
  far = c(sigma = 12, v0 = 0.002))
fit <- fit_allocation(model, observed, starts,
  lower = c(sigma = 0.5, v0 = 1e-6), upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 10),
  output = "flow", loss = "poisson", gradient = TRUE,
  control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8))
summary(fit)
as.data.frame(fit)
```

The summary keeps every start, its convergence, boundaries and messages. All
three starts converge away from the bounds and stop very close to each other,
but the disagreement flag uses deliberately strict default tolerances, so read
the gaps in the per-start table rather than the flag alone. Agreement among the
supplied starts is a numerical check; it does not prove a global optimum or
that the parameters are identified. A σ of about 4.4 minutes means
registration is very local: a practice 9 minutes away keeps only about 12% of
the pull it would have next door.

## Fitted against observed

`fitted()` returns the saved fitted flows; nothing is recomputed. Summing over
small areas gives each practice's modelled registered list.

```{r practice-fit, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4.5}
practices <- data.frame(practice = colnames(observed),
  observed = colSums(observed), fitted = colSums(fitted(fit)))
cor(practices$observed, practices$fitted)
ggplot(practices, aes(observed / 1000, fitted / 1000)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Observed registered residents (thousands)",
    y = "Modelled registered residents (thousands)",
    title = "Practice lists from mainland residents") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The model gives each practice an attraction proportional to its GP FTE and
uses only supply and travel. Practices with more registered patients per GP FTE
than their neighbours therefore have larger observed than modelled lists and
sit below the dashed line.

The outside share is the other observable output. Each small area's modelled
outside share can be compared with the share of its residents registered
outside mainland Cornwall.

```{r outside-map, fig.height = 4.5}
evaluated <- evaluate_allocation(model, coef(fit))
baseline <- predict_allocation(evaluated, travel, demand = demand,
  outputs = c("outside_share", "flow"))
table(baseline$validity$status)
outside <- rbind(
  data.frame(lsoa = names(demand), share = 1 - rowSums(observed) / demand,
    source = "Observed"),
  data.frame(lsoa = names(demand), share = baseline$outputs$outside_share,
    source = "Modelled"))
outside$source <- factor(outside$source, c("Observed", "Modelled"))
outside_map <- merge(cornwall_lsoa[mainland_area, "lsoa"], outside)
ggplot(outside_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = 100 * share), colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~source) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt",
    name = "Registered\noutside (%)") +
  labs(title = "Share of residents registered outside mainland Cornwall") +
  theme_void()
```

`evaluate_allocation()` solves the model once at fixed parameters; it estimates
nothing. `predict_allocation()` then returns the requested outputs for any set
of origins, with separate validity flags. Here `flow` is requested demand times
choice probability, in registered residents. Requested demand only scales the
predicted flows; it never changes the saved practice loads.

Observed registration outside mainland Cornwall is concentrated in a few areas
along the Devon border. A single constant outside weight cannot reproduce that
pattern: the model spreads a small outside share everywhere and puts its largest
values where practices are far away, so treat the modelled outside share as
approximate.

## Predict at new locations

Prediction does not need the fitted small areas. Each cell of the bundled
1 km population grid has its own travel times to every practice, so the saved
model can predict at every populated cell. A `spatial` mapping from requested
origins to raster cells turns one output into a map.

```{r grid-predict}
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
grid_travel <- terra::values(read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif"))
populated <- which(is.finite(terra::values(pop)[, 1]) &
  terra::values(pop)[, 1] > 0)
grid_travel <- grid_travel[populated, colnames(travel)]
rownames(grid_travel) <- paste0("cell", populated)
grid <- predict_allocation(evaluated, grid_travel,
  outputs = c("outside_share", "allocation"))
table(grid$validity$status)
```

Cells on the Isles of Scilly have no travel time to mainland practices, so
their prediction is marked unknown rather than imputed. Inspect these flags
before reading a map.

```{r grid-map, fig.height = 4}
grid_spatial <- list(template = pop,
  cell_index = setNames(populated, rownames(grid_travel)))
grid_outside <- predict_allocation(evaluated, grid_travel,
  outputs = "outside_share", spatial = grid_spatial, type = "raster")
terra::plot(grid_outside, axes = FALSE, col = hcl.colors(50, "Mako", rev = TRUE),
  main = "Modelled outside share (proportion), 1 km grid")
grid_pop <- terra::values(pop)[populated, 1]
far_out <- grid$outputs$outside_share > 0.5
c(cells = sum(far_out, na.rm = TRUE),
  population_percent = round(100 * sum(grid_pop[which(far_out)]) / sum(grid_pop), 2))
```

Some grid cells far from every practice get a high outside share because the
fitted travel scale is short and the outside weight is constant. The
`r sum(far_out, na.rm = TRUE)` cells above 0.5 hold
`r round(100 * sum(grid_pop[which(far_out)]) / sum(grid_pop), 2)`% of the
grid's population, but their values are an
extrapolation of the model, not a measure of unmet need. The grid population
(WorldPop 2020) and the registrations (NHS England 2026) are different sources
and dates, so the grid is used here only for locations.

## Change one practice's supply

A scenario changes the system and evaluates it again at the same parameters.
Here Marazion Surgery is closed by setting its GP FTE to zero; known zero
supply is kept, so the practice stays in the network with no attraction. This
is a model-based, fixed-parameter scenario, not an estimate of what a real
closure would cause: changing supply moves attraction, allocation and every
practice's modelled load together.

```{r scenario}
closed <- "L82047"
gp$name[gp$practice == closed]
scenario_supply <- supply
scenario_supply[closed] <- 0
scenario_model <- clm_allocation(
  prepare_allocation(demand, scenario_supply, travel,
    metadata = cornwall_units),
  family = "gaussian", fit_v0 = TRUE)
scenario <- evaluate_allocation(scenario_model, coef(fit))
changed <- predict_allocation(scenario, travel, demand = demand,
  outputs = c("outside_share", "flow"))
practices$baseline <- colSums(baseline$outputs$flow)
practices$scenario <- colSums(changed$outputs$flow)
practices$change <- practices$scenario - practices$baseline
practices$name <- gp$name[match(practices$practice, gp$practice)]
head(practices[order(-abs(practices$change)),
  c("name", "baseline", "scenario", "change")], 7)
c(outside_change = sum(demand * changed$outputs$outside_share) -
  sum(demand * baseline$outputs$outside_share))
```

The modelled list of the closed practice moves to nearby practices in
Penzance and St Ives Bay, with a small part going to the outside option. Where
a closed practice has no near neighbour, a larger part goes to the outside
option; that follows from the constant outside weight, not from evidence about
where patients would go.

```{r scenario-map, fig.height = 5}
moved <- data.frame(lsoa = names(demand),
  share = baseline$outputs$flow[, closed] / demand)
moved_map <- merge(cornwall_lsoa[mainland_area, "lsoa"], moved)
gained <- merge(cornwall_gp[mainland_gp, "practice"],
  practices[practices$change > 10, c("practice", "change")])
west <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = 130000, ymin = 18000, xmax = 185000,
  ymax = 48000), crs = sf::st_crs(cornwall_lsoa))
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = moved_map, aes(fill = 100 * share), colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.05) +
  geom_sf(data = gained, aes(size = change), shape = 21, fill = "orange") +
  geom_sf(data = cornwall_gp[cornwall_gp$practice == closed, ], shape = 4,
    size = 3, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1,
    name = "Residents at the\nclosed practice (%)") +
  scale_size_area(name = "Modelled\nregistrations\ngained") +
  coord_sf(xlim = west[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = west[c("ymin", "ymax")]) +
  labs(title = "Closing Marazion Surgery (x): who moves and where to",
    subtitle = "Modelled baseline share of residents at the practice; points are receiving practices") +
  theme_void()
```

## Save and reload

The evaluated scenario carries a small prediction snapshot. Saving it does not
keep the model or the travel matrix, and the restored object predicts the same
values.

```{r save-and-reload}
saved <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(scenario, saved)
restored <- readRDS(saved)
stopifnot(identical(
  predict_allocation(restored, travel, demand = demand,
    outputs = c("outside_share", "flow")),
  changed))
unlink(saved)
```

## Facility bootstrap on generated data

The bootstrap is shown on a generated network, not on Cornwall, for three
reasons. Its eligibility rule (all 399 attempts made and at least 380 finite
successful values) was validated on generated designs of this size. A known
truth lets you see whether the intervals cover it. And the method resamples
facility totals treated as independent counts in one period, whereas Cornwall
registrations are a stock of who is registered where; that observation law
would need its own justification before an interval could be read.

The generated network has 80 origins and 40 facilities. Facility totals are
drawn independently from a Poisson law with σ = 12 and v0 = 45. Independence
across facilities is an assumption declared below; it does not follow from
mutually exclusive destinations.

```{r bootstrap-generated-inputs}
units <- list(demand_units = "requests", demand_period = "one_reference_period",
  supply_units = "service_slots", supply_period = "one_reference_period",
  travel_units = "minutes")
i <- seq_len(80)
j <- seq_len(40)
boot_travel <- sqrt(
  outer(seq(2, 58, length.out = 80), seq(4, 56, length.out = 40), "-")^2 +
  outer(8 * sin(i * .73), 7 * sin(j * 1.31), "-")^2) + 2
dimnames(boot_travel) <- list(paste0("origin", i), paste0("facility", j))
boot_demand <- setNames(80 + 35 * (1 + sin(i * .23)), rownames(boot_travel))
boot_supply <- setNames(rep(c(5, 7, 6, 8, 9), 8), colnames(boot_travel))
truth <- c(sigma = 12, v0 = 45)
boot_score <- exp(-boot_travel^2 / (2 * truth[["sigma"]]^2)) *
  rep(boot_supply, each = length(boot_demand))
boot_probability <- boot_score / (rowSums(boot_score) + truth[["v0"]])
set.seed(2490001)
boot_observed <- setNames(rpois(40, colSums(boot_probability * boot_demand)),
  names(boot_supply))
boot_inputs <- prepare_allocation(boot_demand, boot_supply, boot_travel,
  metadata = units)
boot_model <- clm_allocation(boot_inputs, family = "gaussian", fit_v0 = TRUE)
boot_starts <- rbind(short = c(sigma = 8, v0 = 25),
  medium = c(sigma = 15, v0 = 70), wide = c(sigma = 25, v0 = 15))
boot_fit <- fit_allocation(boot_model, boot_observed, boot_starts,
  lower = c(sigma = 2, v0 = 1), upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 500),
  output = "utilization", loss = "poisson", gradient = TRUE,
  control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8))
rbind(truth = truth, estimate = coef(boot_fit))
```

The target here is facility totals (`output = "utilization"`), the observation
unit the bootstrap resamples. The paired scenario raises the second facility's
supply by 20%; each bootstrap draw evaluates baseline and scenario at the same
parameters.

```{r paired-bootstrap-inputs}
boot_scenario_supply <- boot_supply
boot_scenario_supply["facility2"] <- 1.2 * boot_scenario_supply["facility2"]
boot_scenario_inputs <- prepare_allocation(boot_demand, boot_scenario_supply,
  boot_travel, metadata = units)
boot_scenario <- clm_allocation(boot_scenario_inputs, family = "gaussian",
  fit_v0 = TRUE)
observation <- list(event = "allocated service requests",
  period = "one_reference_period", sampling = "independent_facilities")
rebuild_boot <- identical(Sys.getenv("SPAX_REBUILD_VIGNETTE_BOOTSTRAP"), "true")
```

```{r paired-bootstrap, eval = rebuild_boot}
boot <- bootstrap_allocation(boot_model, boot_fit, observation,
  scenario = boot_scenario, seed = 20260930)
```

### Precomputed bootstrap result

The chunk above is the exact call, but its 399 attempts take about three
minutes, so it is not run while this guide is built. Its unmodified result is
stored in `allocation-bootstrap.rds`, regenerated by
`data-raw/precompute-vignette-bootstrap.R`, which renders this guide with
`SPAX_REBUILD_VIGNETTE_BOOTSTRAP=true` so that the chunk runs live and saves its
result. Nothing is subsampled or summarized; run the chunk yourself to
reproduce it. The checks below confirm that the stored result matches the
inputs and fit computed live here and that all 399 attempts were made.

```{r paired-bootstrap-load}
boot_file <- "allocation-bootstrap.rds"
if (rebuild_boot) {
  attr(boot, "spax_version") <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("spax"))
  saveRDS(boot, boot_file, compress = "xz")
}
boot <- readRDS(boot_file)
stopifnot(inherits(boot, "ae_allocation_bootstrap"),
  boot$seed == 20260930L, boot$planned == 399L, boot$attempted == 399L,
  identical(boot$facility_ids, names(boot_supply)),
  identical(boot$observation, observation),
  identical(boot$input_metadata, units),
  isTRUE(all.equal(boot$original$theta, coef(boot_fit), tolerance = 1e-6)))
c(status = boot$status, attempted = boot$attempted, successful = boot$successful,
  built_with_spax = attr(boot, "spax_version"),
  running_spax = as.character(utils::packageVersion("spax")))
```

```{r paired-bootstrap-results}
parameters <- c("sigma", "v0")
estimates <- as.data.frame(boot)
estimates[estimates$quantity %in% parameters, ]
draws <- as.data.frame(boot, type = "draws")
head(draws[c("attempt", "status", parameters)])
```

The procedure makes 399 predetermined attempts. It resamples facility
observations while keeping every facility and its supply in the allocation.
Failed attempts are kept and not replaced, and successful fits on an inner
boundary stay in the distribution. An interval is reported only when all 399
attempts were made, at least 380 values are finite and the original fit is
eligible; otherwise the result keeps its point estimates and reasons but
withholds intervals.

The tables above show the two model parameters; the saved result also holds
regional and paired-scenario quantities, listed by `as.data.frame(boot)`.

```{r bootstrap-truth, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
for (q in c("sigma", "v0")) {
  plot(boot, quantity = q, main = paste(q, "(dashed line: truth)"))
  abline(v = truth[[q]], col = "orange", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
}
par(oldpar)
```

In this generated design both intervals contain the true values (dashed). They
are pointwise percentile intervals conditional on the declared observation law
and on fixed demand, supply, travel and facilities. Acceptance in generated
studies does not establish an application's observation law or guarantee exact
95% coverage, and the paired scenario is model-based, not causal.

## Export and reload in a fresh session

CSV files make saved tables available to other software but drop R classes and
attributes. Keep an RDS bundle alongside them to preserve the fit, declarations,
units and the complete results.

```{r export-saved-results}
export_dir <- tempfile("allocation-results-")
dir.create(export_dir)
export_tables <- list(parameters = as.data.frame(fit),
  practices = practices,
  bootstrap_estimates = as.data.frame(boot),
  bootstrap_draws = as.data.frame(boot, type = "draws"),
  bootstrap_starts = as.data.frame(boot, type = "starts"))
for (name in names(export_tables)) {
  write.csv(export_tables[[name]], file.path(export_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")),
    row.names = FALSE)
}
bundle_path <- file.path(export_dir, "allocation-results.rds")
saveRDS(list(fit = fit, scenario = scenario, bootstrap = boot,
  closed = closed, tables = export_tables), bundle_path)
list.files(export_dir)
```

Finally, a new R process with the installed package reads the bundle. It checks
the saved tables, predicts the scenario again from the bundled Cornwall travel
times, and prints and plots the saved results without refitting or drawing a
new bootstrap sample.

```{r fresh-installed-reload}
child_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
literal <- function(x) paste(capture.output(dput(x)), collapse = "\n")
writeLines(c(
  paste0(".libPaths(c(", literal(dirname(find.package("spax"))), ", .libPaths()))"),
  "library(spax)",
  paste0("saved <- readRDS(", literal(bundle_path), ")"),
  "stopifnot(identical(as.data.frame(saved$fit), saved$tables$parameters))",
  "stopifnot(identical(as.data.frame(saved$bootstrap), saved$tables$bootstrap_estimates))",
  "stopifnot(identical(as.data.frame(saved$bootstrap, type = 'draws'), saved$tables$bootstrap_draws))",
  "stopifnot(identical(as.data.frame(saved$bootstrap, type = 'starts'), saved$tables$bootstrap_starts))",
  "areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)",
  "gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)",
  "travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa[!areas$scilly], gp$practice[!gp$scilly]]",
  "demand <- setNames(areas$registered[!areas$scilly], areas$lsoa[!areas$scilly])",
  "flow <- predict_allocation(saved$scenario, travel, demand = demand, outputs = 'flow')$outputs$flow",
  "stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(colSums(flow)), unname(saved$tables$practices$scenario))))",
  "stopifnot(colSums(flow)[[saved$closed]] == 0)",
  "stopifnot(inherits(summary(saved$fit), 'summary.ae_multistart_fit'))",
  "stopifnot(inherits(summary(saved$bootstrap), 'summary.ae_allocation_bootstrap'))",
  "print(summary(saved$fit))",
  "print(summary(saved$bootstrap))",
  "plot_path <- tempfile(fileext = '.pdf')",
  "grDevices::pdf(plot_path)",
  "plot(saved$fit, type = 'fit')",
  "plot(saved$bootstrap, quantity = 'sigma')",
  "plot(saved$bootstrap, quantity = 'sigma', type = 'draws')",
  "grDevices::dev.off()",
  "stopifnot(file.info(plot_path)$size > 0)",
  "unlink(plot_path)",
  "cat('Fresh installed saved-result inspection passed\\n')"
), child_path)
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") "Rscript.exe" else "Rscript")
status <- system2(rscript, c("--vanilla", shQuote(child_path)))
stopifnot(status == 0L)
unlink(child_path)
```

## Sources

Registrations and workforce: NHS England, Open Government Licence v3.0.
Boundaries and centroids: Office for National Statistics, Open Government
Licence v3.0; contains OS data. Population grid: WorldPop 2020, Creative
Commons Attribution 4.0. Travel times are derived from the Malaria Atlas
Project motorised friction surface (Weiss et al. 2020, Creative Commons
Attribution). Full attributions: `system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax")`.
